text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service `inference-prod` -> escalation policy `infra-night` (page_count=1)

maria: i just got the page, looks like infra-oncall got it but this should have gone to model-serving-oncall

bob: seeing same, traffic graphs show a spike in 5xx from the inference frontend around 02:14 UTC

carla: grabbing PD console. which service id?

maria: service name `inference-prod`, PD ID shows `svc_0a1b2c` in the alert payload

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident INC123456 created -> routed to escalation `infra-night` (escalation_id:e_9876)

carla: odd — the service tag in our infra repo is `team:model-serving` but PD lookup returns `team:infra`. might be a tag-sync issue after yesterday's deploy

maria: can we stop pages to infra while we triage? they're awake and this isn't their responsibility

bob: suggest setting the PD service to maintenance or temporarily reassigning the escalation. quick option: change the service's escalation policy to model-serving and trigger a test page.

carla: i'm going to try a reassignment. running PD CLI: 
```
pd service update svc_0a1b2c --escalation-policy epi_modelserving_01
```
carla: running...

carla: update succeeded. now triggering test page to verify routing

pagerduty-bot: Test page sent to escalation `model-serving` -> oncall: bob (model-serving-oncall)

bob: got the test page. routing fixed for tests. i'll keep monitoring live traffic and throttle pages if noise returns

maria: quick smoke: running `curl` against /v1/generate for sample keys — seeing 10-20% increased latency and occasional 503s for a small subset of shard ids

bob: pulling KG logs, it looks like a cache layer (prefix cache) started returning misses due to a memcached eviction storm around the same time as tag-sync job at 02:10

maria: so two simultaneous events: tag-sync changed PD metadata, and memcache eviction caused upstream errors -> both combined created the noisy page to wrong team

dave: customer impact? any live customer errors or degradation on SLA?

maria: partial — a handful of high-throughput customers saw elevated error rates for ~3m. we have traces for 4 customers with >5% error spikes

carla: i'll open a support blast to the affected customer owners (cc: @dave) and include ETA for follow-up.

bob: tactical mitigations in place: 1) PD service escalation corrected 2) memcache eviction pressure reduced by increasing max_item_size and bumping TTLs for critical prefixes 3) enabling fallback KV cache on model-serving nodes

maria: commands run: 
```
# bump critical TTLs
redis-cli -h cache-primary CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
# enable fallback config
kubectl -n infra set configmap model-serving-config --from-literal=use_kv_fallback=true
```

maria: monitoring shows error rate trending down to baseline (02:22 UTC)

pagerduty-bot: INC123456 acknowledged by maria

carla: we should add a safety check: a CI job that validates PD service tags after each infra deploy. i'll file a ticket

dave: agreed. also add an alert that flags when service escalation policy changes outside of approved repo commits

maria: temp postmortem notes: root cause = tag-sync drift after deploy + memcache eviction storm causing customer errors -> wrong escalation target. Mitigations: PD reassignment, cache config fixes, monitoring and support notifications.

carla: ticket created -> RED-3421 "PD tags drift detection + protection". assigning to carla and infra-sre

bob: follow-up actions: 1) add acceptance test in deploy pipeline to verify service->escalation mapping 2) add PD webhook that alerts on mapping changes 3) run a tabletop in next oncall rotation

maria: marking resolved for paging. will circle back with root cause doc + timeline tomorrow. closing thread once support notifies customers. :white_check_mark:
